headline: NYC Plants 18,261 Trees in Single Year, Most Since 2016
meta_description: Mamdani's first year in office brought record tree planting to New York City, with most trees going to neighborhoods facing extreme heat.
summary_short: NYC planted 18,261 trees in a single fiscal year under Mamdani—the most since 2016—prioritizing neighborhoods most vulnerable to extreme heat.
body:
New York City planted 18,261 trees in a single fiscal year under Mamdani's leadership, marking the highest annual total since 2016. The ambitious effort represents a strategic shift in how the city approaches climate resilience and urban cooling.

What makes this achievement significant is where those trees went. Rather than spreading plantings evenly across the city, most were concentrated in neighborhoods most vulnerable to extreme heat. These are often the same areas with less existing tree canopy, fewer parks, and higher rates of heat-related illness during summer months.

The shade from newly planted trees brings immediate benefits—cooler streets, reduced energy costs for nearby residents, and improved air quality. For neighborhoods that have historically received fewer resources, this planting campaign represents tangible progress toward a more equitable city.
quick_facts: 18,261 trees planted in one fiscal year under Mamdani
Majority planted in heat-vulnerable NYC neighborhoods
